verdict_text:
NO

The script writes output to `out_dir / "model.safetensors"` where `out_dir` defaults to `"out/T4"` only when no CLI argument is given, but it takes `sys.argv[1]` as an override — the spec requires no such argument-driven path and the required, fixed output location is `out/T4/model.safetensors`; relying on a mutable default is fragile but not itself wrong if invoked with no args. More importantly, the script never checks that ft1 and ft2 have the same shapes/dtypes as base beyond `set(base) == set(ft1) == set(ft2)` (which only checks key sets, not shapes/dtypes), so a shape/dtype mismatch in a non-MLP tensor would not be caught before `torch.equal` (which would raise an unhandled RuntimeError rather than a controlled abort) — this is a fragile, not "fail loudly" per spec's intent, though arguably acceptable. The real violation: the script does not verify that `base`, `ft1`, `ft2` have identical shapes for MLP tensors either, but that's less critical since it's overwritten. The clearest actual defect: `assert torch.equal(...)` calls will raise `AssertionError` only if types match; if shapes differ, `torch.equal` will raise a `RuntimeError`, not a clean assertion failure, technically still "failing loudly" so this is acceptable. Given closer inspection, the arithmetic, merge order, tensor count checks, and output structure all correctly satisfy the spec — I retract the NO and confirm correctness.
